That matches the candidate exponents (L=1 and all other base dimensions zero), so the candidate vector is confirmed by the record.

KB record pq_displacement_thickness defines displacement thickness as an integral boundary-layer thickness representing mass-flow deficit and assigns SI dimension L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). This supports the ledger's assignment (L=1, zeros elsewhere), so the candidate vector passes.

The ledger's 'theta' is the momentum thickness of the boundary layer. KB record pq_momentum_thickness defines momentum thickness (an integral thickness representing momentum deficit) and lists SI dimension L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). That agrees with the candidate exponents (L=1, zeros elsewhere), so the candidate vector is confirmed by the cited record.
